paras.en: Is comprehension the same whether a person reads a text onscreen or on paper?
And are listening to and viewing content as effective as reading the written word when covering the same material?
The answers to both questions are often “no”.
The reasons relate to a variety of factors, including reduced concentration, an entertainment mindset (心态) and a tendency to multitask while consuming digital content.
When reading texts of several hundred words or more, learning is generally more successful when it’s on paper than onscreen.
A large amount of research confirms this finding.

The benefits of print reading particularly shine through when experimenters move from posing simple tasks — like identifying the main idea in a reading passage — to ones that require mental abstraction — such as drawing inferences from a text.
The differences between print and digital reading results are partly related to paper’s physical properties.
With paper, there is a literal laying on of hands, along with the visual geography of distinct pages.
People often link their memory of what they’ve read to how far into the book it was or where it was on the page.
But equally important is the mental aspect.
Reading researchers have proposed a theory called “shallowing hypothesis (假说)”.
According to this theory, people approach digital texts with a mindset suited to social media, which are often not so serious, and devote less mental effort than when they are reading print.
Audio (音频) and video can feel more engaging than text, and so university teachers increasingly turn to these technologies — say, assigning an online talk instead of an article by the same person.
However, psychologists have demonstrated that when adults read news stories, they remember more of the content than if they listen to or view identical pieces.
Digital texts, audio and video all have educational roles, especially when providing resources not available in print.
However, for maximizing learning where mental focus and reflection are called for, educators shouldn’t assume all media are the same, even when they contain identical words.

passages.name: 2024 全国新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读D

paras.en: In the race to document the species on Earth before they go extinct, researchers and citizen scientists have collected billions of records.
Today, most records of biodiversity are often in the form of photos, videos, and other digital records.
Though they are useful for detecting shifts in the number and variety of species in an area, a new Stanford study has found that this type of record is not perfect.

“With the rise of technology it is easy for people to make observations of different species with the aid of a mobile application,” said Barnabas Daru, who is lead author of the study and assistant professor of biology in the Stanford School of Humanities and Sciences.

“These observations now outnumber the primary data that comes from physical specimens (标本), and since we are increasingly using observational data to investigate how species are responding to global change, I wanted to know: Are they usable?”
Using a global dataset of 1.9 billion records of plants, insects, birds, and animals, Daru and his team tested how well these data represent actual global biodiversity patterns.

“We were particularly interested in exploring the aspects of sampling that tend to bias (使有偏差) data, like the greater likelihood of a citizen scientist to take a picture of a flowering plant instead of the grass right next to it,” said Daru.
Their study revealed that the large number of observation-only records did not lead to better global coverage.
Moreover, these data are biased and favor certain regions, time periods, and species.
This makes sense because the people who get observational biodiversity data on mobile devices are often citizen scientists recording their encounters with species in areas nearby.
These data are also biased toward certain species with attractive or eye-catching features.
What can we do with the imperfect datasets of biodiversity?
“Quite a lot,” Daru explained.
“Biodiversity apps can use our study results to inform users of oversampled areas and lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled.
To improve the quality of observational data, biodiversity apps can also encourage users to have an expert confirm the identification of their uploaded image.”

passages.name: 2024 全国新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读C

paras.en: We all know fresh is best when it comes to food.
However, most produce at the store went through weeks of travel and covered hundreds of miles before reaching the table.
While farmer’s markets are a solid choice to reduce the journey, Babylon Micro-Farm (BMF) shortens it even more.
BMF is an indoor garden system.
It can be set up for a family.
Additionally, it could serve a larger audience such as a hospital, restaurant or school.
The innovative design requires little effort to achieve a reliable weekly supply of fresh greens.
Specifically, it’s a farm that relies on new technology.
By connecting through the Cloud, BMF is remotely monitored.
Also, there is a convenient app that provides growing data in real time.
Because the system is automated, it significantly reduces the amount of water needed to grow plants.
Rather than watering rows of soil, the system provides just the right amount to each plant.
After harvest, users simply replace the plants with a new pre-seeded pod (容器) to get the next growth cycle started.
Moreover, having a system in the same building where it’s eaten means zero emissions (排放) from transporting plants from soil to salad.
In addition, there’s no need for pesticides and other chemicals that pollute traditional farms and the surrounding environment.
BMF employees live out sustainability in their everyday lives.
About half of them walk or bike to work.
Inside the office, they encourage recycling and waste reduction by limiting garbage cans and avoiding single-use plastic.
“We are passionate about reducing waste, carbon and chemicals in our environment,” said a BMF employee.

paras.en: Given the astonishing potential of AI to transform our lives we all need to take action to deal with our AI-powered future, and this is where AI by Design: A Plan for Living with Artificial Intelligence comes in.
This absorbing new book by Catriona Campbell is a practical roadmap addressing the challenges posed by the forthcoming AI revolution (变革).

In the wrong hands, such a book could prove as complicated to process as the computer code (代码) that powers AI but, thankfully, Campbell has more than two decades’ professional experience translating the heady into the understandable.

She writes from the practical angle of a business person rather than as an academic, making for a guide which is highly accessible and informative and which, by the close, will make you feel almost as smart as AI.
As we soon come to learn from AI by Design, AI is already super-smart and will become more capable, moving from the current generation of “narrow-AI” to Artificial General Intelligence.
From there, Campbell says, will come Artificial Dominant Intelligence.
This is why Campbell has set out to raise awareness of AI and its future now — several decades before these developments are expected to take place.
She says it is essential that we keep control of artificial intelligence, or risk being sidelined and perhaps even worse.
Campbell’s point is to wake up those responsible for AI — the technology companies and world leaders-so they are on the same page as all the experts currently developing it.
She explains we are at a “tipping point” in history and must act now to prevent an extinction-level event for humanity.
We need to consider how we want our future with AI to pan out.
Such structured thinking, followed by global regulation, will enable us to achieve greatness rather than our downfall.
AI will affect us all, and if you only read one book on the subject, this is it.
The Saint Lukas train doesn’t accept passengers — it accepts only the sick.
The Saint Lukas is one of five government-sponsored medical trains that travel to remote towns in central and eastern Russia.
Each stop lasts an average of two days, and during that time the doctors and nurses on board provide rural (乡村) populations with basic medical care, X-ray scans and prescriptions.

“People started queuing to make an appointment early in the morning,” says Emile Ducke, a German photographer who traveled with the staff of the Saint Lukas for a two-week trip in November through the vast regions (区域) of Krasnoyarsk and Khakassia.
Russia’s public health care service has been in serious need of modernization.

The government has struggled to come up with measures to address the problem, particularly in the poorer, rural areas east of the Volga River, including arranging doctor’s appointments by video chat and expanding financial aid programs to motivate doctors to practice medicine in remote parts of the country like Krasnoyarsk.
The annual arrival of the Saint Lukas is another attempt to improve the situation.
For 10 months every year, the train stops at about eight stations over two weeks, before returning to the regional capital to refuel and restock (补给).
Then it starts all over again the next month.
Most stations wait about a year between visits.
Doctors see up to 150 patients every day.
The train’s equipment allows for basic checkups.
“I was very impressed by the doctors and their assistants working and living in such little space but still staying focused and very concerned,” says Ducke.
“They were the best chance for many rural people to get the treatment they want.”
“I didn’t like the ending,” I said to my favorite college professor.
It was my junior year of undergraduate, and I was doing an independent study on Victorian literature.
I had just finished reading The Mill on the Floss by George Eliot, and I was heartbroken with the ending.
Prof. Gracie, with all his patience, asked me to think about it beyond whether I liked it or not.

He suggested I think about the difference between endings that I wanted for the characters and endings that were right for the characters, endings that satisfied the story even if they didn’t have a traditionally positive outcome.
Of course, I would have preferred a different ending for Tom and Maggie Tulliver, but the ending they got did make the most sense for them.
This was an aha moment for me, and I never thought about endings the same way again.
From then on, if I wanted to read an ending guaranteed to be happy, I’d pick up a love romance.
If I wanted an ending I couldn’t guess, I’d pick up a mystery (悬疑小说).
One where I kind of knew what was going to happen, historical fiction.
Choosing what to read became easier.
But writing the end — that’s hard.
It’s hard for writers because endings carry so much weight with readers.
You have to balance creating an ending that’s unpredictable, but doesn’t seem to come from nowhere, one that fits what’s right for the characters.
That’s why this issue (期) of Writer’s Digest aims to help you figure out how to write the best ending for whatever kind of writing you’re doing.
If it’s short stories, Peter Mountford breaks down six techniques you can try to see which one helps you stick the landing.
Elizabeth Sims analyzes the final chapters of five great novels to see what key points they include and how you can adapt them for your work.
This issue won’t tell you what your ending should be — that’s up to you and the story you’re telling — but it might provide what you need to get there.
The notion that we live in someone else’s video game is irresistible to many.
Searching the term “simulation hypothesis” (模拟假说) returns numerous results that debate whether the universe is a computer simulation — a concept that some scientists actually take seriously.
Unfortunately, this is not a scientific question.
We will probably never know whether it’s true.
We can, instead, use this idea to advance scientific knowledge.
The 18th-century philosopher Kant argued that the universe ultimately consists of things-in-themselves that are unknowable.
While he held the notion that objective reality exists, he said our mind plays a necessary role in structuring and shaping our perceptions.
Modern sciences have revealed that our perceptual experience of the world is the result of many stages of processing by sensory systems and cognitive (认知的) functions in the brain.
No one knows exactly what happens within this black box.

If empirical (实证的) experience fails to reveal reality, reasoning won’t reveal reality either since it relies on concepts and words that are contingent on our social, cultural and psychological histories.
Again, a black box.
So, if we accept that the universe is unknowable, we also accept we will never know if we live in a computer simulation.
And then, we can shift our inquiry from “Is the universe a computer simulation?” to “Can we model the universe as a computer simulation?”
Modelling reality is what we do.
To facilitate our comprehension of the world, we build models based on conceptual metaphors (隐喻) that are familiar to us.
In Newton’s era, we imagined the universe as a clock.
In Einstein’s, we uncovered the standard model of particle (粒子) physics.
Now that we are in the information age, we have new concepts such as the computer, information processing, virtual reality, and simulation.
Unsurprisingly, these new concepts inspire us to build new models of the universe.
Models are not the reality, however.
There is no point in arguing if the universe is a clock, a set of particles or an output of computation.
All these models are tools to deal with the unknown and to make discoveries.
And the more tools we have, the more effective and insightful we can become.
It can be imagined that comparable to the process of building previous scientific models, developing the “computer simulation” metaphor-based model will also be a hugely rewarding exercise.
Franz Boas’s description of Inuit (因纽特人) life in the 19th century illustrates the probable moral code of early humans.
Here, norms (规范) were unwritten and rarely expressed clearly, but were well understood and taken to heart.
Dishonest and violent behaviours were disapproved of; leadership, marriage and interactions with other groups were loosely governed by traditions.
Conflict was often resolved in musical battles.
Because arguing angrily leads to chaos, it was strongly discouraged.
With life in the unforgiving Northern Canada being so demanding, the Inuit’s practical approach to morality made good sense.
The similarity of moral virtues across cultures is striking, even though the relative ranking of the virtues may vary with a social group’s history and environment.
Typically, cruelty and cheating are discouraged, while cooperation, humbleness and courage are praised.
These universal norms far pre-date the concept of any moralising religion or written law.
Instead, they are rooted in the similarity of basic human needs and our shared mechanisms for learning and problem solving.
Our social instincts (本能) include the intense desire to belong.
The approval of others is rewarding, while their disapproval is strongly disliked.
These social emotions prepare our brains to shape our behaviour according to the norms and values of our family and our community.
More generally, social instincts motivate us to learn how to behave in a socially complex world.
The mechanism involves a repurposed reward system originally used to develop habits important for self-care.
Our brains use the system to acquire behavioural patterns regarding safe routes home, efficient food gathering and dangers to avoid.
Good habits save time, energy and sometimes your life.
Good social habits do something similar in a social context.
We learn to tell the truth, even when lying is self-serving; we help a grandparent even when it is inconvenient.
We acquire what we call a sense of right and wrong.
Social benefits are accompanied by social demands: we must get along, but not put up with too much.
Hence self-discipline is advantageous.
In humans, a greatly enlarged brain boosts self-control, just as it boosts problem-solving skills in the social as well as the physical world.
These abilities are strengthened by our capacity for language, which allows social practices to develop in extremely unobvious ways.

passages.name: 2024 天津卷（第一次·3月） 阅读C

paras.en: Our teacher, Miss Chevalier was a small woman, with a moon face, fatty fingers and curls that sprang straight up from her head, hence the funny name “Poodle (卷毛狗)”.
She taught in our reading club.
Sometimes she would look in and ask what we were reading — not to check but to know.
That’s what happened the day my club was reading aloud a poem by Henry Longfellow.
I guess I was better than the others, for Miss Chevalier asked a while later, “Addie, I was wondering if you would recite the whole poem to the Saturday evening’s club.”
She said a famous professor was going to give a lecture about the poet, and a presentation of that poem would be a fresh way to start.
She asked me to memorize it.
“But that shouldn’t be a problem for a child of your ability,” she added.
I’m telling you, my happy feet barely touched the ground all the way home.
To me, that was the biggest thing ever and I soon learned the whole poem by heart, well prepared for our first rehearsal.
I was desperately nervous when I went to her office the next day.
But the good thing was she always had the smile that would make you feel like you just did something right.
Halfway through the poem, Miss Chevalier stopped me and asked if I knew what “impetuous” meant.
Despite her encouraging smile, I wanted to sink through the floor because I was unsure about its pronunciation as well as its meaning.
Miss Chevalier pretended not to have noticed my red face and handed me a dictionary, asking me to read its definition aloud.
“Impetuous has two definitions: rushing with great force or violence; acting suddenly, with little thought.”
She asked me which one fitted the poem.
I read both definitions over again, trying to figure it out, but Miss Chevalier must have read my mind.
“There is no wrong answer,” she said, “I want to know your opinion, Addie.”
Hesitantly, I said, “Maybe… both.”
She liked that.
“One has to be impetuous both ways or they wouldn’t dare to face up to any challenge.
Would you call yourself impetuous?”
I knew she was asking for an opinion.
“My mother thinks being impetuous for girls is improper, anyway.”
She said my mom was somewhat right about that.
“But girls should also be wise to take up challenges when needed.
I believe you are such a girl.”
After that, I would never call Miss Chevalier “Poodle” again.

paras.en: Research sometimes proves, with data, what we more or less already know (e.g. exercise is good for you, and polluted air isn’t).
Still, sometimes our assumptions are incorrect, and scientific findings surprise researchers, along with the rest of us.
A recent example is the phenomenon of disappearing lakes in parts of the frozen treeless Arctic (北极的) region.
You might think these lakes would be expanding, not disappearing.
As climate change warms the region — melting (融化) surface snow and ice as well as the permafrost (永冻层)— there should be more surface water, forming larger lakes and even new ones.
Recently, however, scientists have observed not just shrinking (缩小的) lakes but lakes that have completely gone away.
Many scientists shared the commonsense expectation that as permafrost melted, lakes would at first expand with meltwater flowing into them.
Eventually, researchers made a prediction that progressive warming during the 21st and 22nd centuries would dry out the Arctic, and lakes would begin to shrink.
But now it looks as if Arctic lakes are disappearing a century sooner than predicted.
A case in point is that some large, age-old lakes shrank dramatically in what appears to have been a matter of months.
Scientists have labeled this phenomenon “disastrous lake loss”.
What caused this?
The frozen solid ground actually contains bits of rock, mineral and organic matter, leaving spaces in between.
And because these spaces are filled with solid ice, liquid water cannot readily get inside, but it can when the permafrost melts, allowing more water to get through.
Soon after that, around 192 lakes in northwestern Alaska are gone from sight.
Why did scientists miss this?
One probable reason is that most climate models assume that the melting of permafrost is driven only by warming air.
New evidence suggests, however, that rainfall — particularly increasing autumn rain — is now contributing significantly to permafrost loss.
The rainfall carries heat into the ground.
Yet none of the existing models includes such processes.
That is a good example of why — no matter how complex our models are or may one day be — we need direct observation of the natural world.
On September 7, 1991, the costliest hailstorm (雹暴) in Canadian history hit Calgary’s southern suburbs.
As a result, since 1996 a group of insurance companies have spent about $2 million per year on the Alberta Hail Suppression Project.
Airplanes seed threatening storm cells with a chemical to make small ice crystals fall as rain before they can grow into dangerous hailstones.
But farmers in east-central Alberta — downwind of the hail project flights — worry that precious moisture (水分) is being stolen from their thirsty land by the cloud seeding.
Norman Stienwand, who farms in that area, has been addressing public meetings on this issue for years.

“Basically, the provincial government is letting the insurance companies protect the Calgary-Edmonton urban area from hail,” Mr. Stienwand says, “but they’re increasing drought risk as far east as Saskatchewan.”
The Alberta hail project is managed by Terry Krauss, a cloud physicist who works for Weather Modification Inc. of Fargo, North Dakota.
“We affect only a very small percentage of the total moisture in the air, so we cannot be causing drought.”
Dr. Krauss says.
“In fact, we may be helping increase the moisture downwind by creating wetter ground.”
One doubter about the safety of cloud seeding is Chuck Doswell, a research scientist who just retired from the University of Oklahoma.
“In 1999, I personally saw significant tornadoes (龙卷风) form from a seeded storm cell in Kansas,” Dr. Doswell says.
“Does cloud seeding create killer storms or reduce moisture downwind?
No one really knows, of course, but the seeding goes on.”
Given the degree of doubt, Mr. Stienwand suggests, “it would be wise to stop cloud seeding.”
In practice, doubt has had the opposite effect.
Due to the lack of scientific proof concerning their impacts, no one has succeeded in winning a lawsuit against cloud-seeding companies.
Hence, private climate engineering can proceed in relative legal safety.
The Stanford marshmallow (棉花糖) test was originally conducted by psychologist Walter Mischel in the late 1960s.
Children aged four to six at a nursery school were placed in a room.
A single sugary treat, selected by the child, was placed on a table.
Each child was told if they waited for 15 minutes before eating the treat, they would be given a second treat.
Then they were left alone in the room.
Follow-up studies with the children later in life showed a connection between an ability to wait long enough to obtain a second treat and various forms of success.
As adults we face a version of the marshmallow test every day.

We’re not tempted (诱惑) by sugary treats, but by our computers, phones, and tablets — all the devices that connect us to the global delivery system for various types of information that do to us what marshmallows do to preschoolers.

We are tempted by sugary treats because our ancestors lived in a calorie-poor world, and our brains developed a response mechanism to these treats that reflected their value — a feeling of reward and satisfaction.

But as we’ve reshaped the world around us, dramatically reducing the cost and effort involved in obtaining calories, we still have the same brains we had thousands of years ago, and this mismatch is at the heart of why so many of us struggle to resist tempting foods that we know we shouldn’t eat.
A similar process is at work in our response to information.
Our formative environment as a species was information-poor, so our brains developed a mechanism that prized new information.
But global connectivity has greatly changed our information environment.
We are now ceaselessly bombarded (轰炸) with new information.

Therefore, just as we need to be more thoughtful about our caloric consumption, we also need to be more thoughtful about our information consumption, resisting the temptation of the mental “junk food” in order to manage our time most effectively.

passages.name: 2025 全国一卷 阅读C
passages.title: 把街道还给行人
passages.genre: 说明文 · 书评与城市生活
passages.summary: 近年来街道的安全性或许有所改善，但行人（尤其是儿童）的出行能力却在下降，许多家长因路上车太多、孩子步行不安全而改为开车送孩子上学。两位荷兰作者在新书《出行》中呼吁重新思考街道的作用。几十年前，城市就开始围绕汽车重新规划，简·雅各布斯等人曾发起抗争；如今澳大利亚的汽车拥有率位居世界前列。本文作者赞同《出行》两位作者的观点：是时候换个角度看待家门口的街道了。

paras.en: While safety improvements might have been made to our streets in recent years, transport studies also show declines in pedestrian (行人) mobility, especially among young children.
paras.zh: 虽然近年来我们的街道在安全方面可能有所改善，但交通研究也显示，行人的出行能力在下降，在年幼的孩子中尤为明显。

paras.en: Many parents say there’s too much traffic on the roads for their children to walk safely to school, so they pack them into the car instead.
paras.zh: 许多家长说，路上车太多，孩子没法安全地步行上学，所以他们改为开车送孩子。

paras.en: Dutch authors Thalia Verkade and Marco te Brömmelstroet are bothered by facts like these.
paras.zh: 荷兰作者塔利娅·费尔卡德和马尔科·特·布罗梅尔斯特鲁特对这样的事实感到困扰。

paras.en: In their new book Movement: How to Take Back Our Streets and Transform Our Lives, they call for a rethink of our streets and the role they play in our lives.
paras.zh: 在他们的新书《出行：如何夺回我们的街道，改变我们的生活》中，他们呼吁重新思考我们的街道，以及街道在我们生活中所扮演的角色。

paras.en: Life on city streets started to change decades ago.
paras.zh: 城市街道上的生活早在几十年前就开始改变了。

paras.en: Whole neighbourhoods were destroyed to make way for new road networks and kids had to play elsewhere.
paras.zh: 整片整片的街区被拆毁，为新的道路网络让路，孩子们只好到别处去玩。

paras.en: Some communities fought back.
paras.zh: 一些社区奋起反抗。

paras.en: Most famously, a Canadian journalist who had moved her family to Manhattan in the early 1950s led a campaign to stop the destruction of her local park.
paras.zh: 最有名的是，一位在20世纪50年代初举家搬到曼哈顿的加拿大记者领导了一场运动，阻止当地公园被毁。

paras.en: Describing her alarm at its proposed replacement with an expressway, Jane Jacobs called on her mayor (市长) to champion “New York as a decent place to live, and not just rush through.”
paras.zh: 简·雅各布斯表达了她对有人提议用高速公路取代这座公园的担忧，呼吁市长捍卫“纽约作为一个宜居之地，而不只是一个匆匆路过的地方”。

w.m: adj. 像样的；令人满意的

paras.en: Similar campaigns occurred in Australia in the late 1960s and 1970s as well.
paras.zh: 20世纪60年代末和70年代，澳大利亚也发生过类似的运动。

paras.en: Although these campaigns were widespread, the reality is that the majority of the western cities were completely redesigned around the needs of the motor car.
paras.zh: 尽管这些运动很普遍，但现实是，大多数西方城市都完全围绕汽车的需要重新设计了。

paras.en: The number of cars on roads has been increasing rapidly.
paras.zh: 路上的汽车数量一直在迅速增加。

paras.en: In Australia we now have over twenty million cars for just over twenty-six million people, among the highest rate of car ownership in the world.
paras.zh: 在澳大利亚，如今我们2600万出头的人口拥有2000多万辆汽车，汽车拥有率位居世界前列。

paras.en: We invest a lot in roads that help us rush through, but we fail to account for the true costs.
paras.zh: 我们在能让我们匆匆通过的道路上投入很多，却没有把真正的代价考虑在内。

paras.en: Do we really recognise what it costs us as a society when children can’t move safely around our communities?
paras.zh: 当孩子们无法在社区里安全走动时，我们真的意识到这让整个社会付出了什么代价吗？

paras.en: The authors of Movement have it right: it’s time to think differently about that street outside your front door.
paras.zh: 《出行》的作者说得对：是时候换个角度看待你家门外的那条街了。

passages.name: 2025 全国一卷 阅读D
passages.title: 把自来水煮沸再过滤，可去除大部分微塑料
passages.genre: 说明文 · 健康与环境
passages.summary: 微塑料已遍布地球，甚至出现在人体内。中国研究人员发现，把自来水煮沸五分钟、冷却后过滤，可以去除至少80%的微塑料；其效果取决于水中碳酸钙的含量，硬水效果最好。研究也有局限，只考察了三种常见塑料。这些发现为减少微塑料摄入提供了一条可能的途径；一位未参与研究的专家肯定了该研究的方法，并认为应考虑升级饮用水处理厂。

paras.en: Microplastics have become a common source of pollution across the Earth — they have settled in the deep sea and on the Himalayas, stuck inside volcanic rocks, filled the stomachs of seabirds and even fallen in fresh Antarctic snow.
paras.zh: 微塑料已成为地球上常见的污染源——它们沉积在深海和喜马拉雅山上，嵌在火山岩里，填满了海鸟的胃，甚至落在南极新下的雪中。

paras.en: They are even appearing inside humans.
paras.zh: 它们甚至出现在人体内。

paras.en: Now, new research suggests that a simple, cheap measure may significantly reduce the level of microplastics in water from your tap (水龙头): boiling and filtering (过滤) it.
paras.zh: 现在，新的研究表明，一个简单又便宜的方法或许能大大降低自来水中的微塑料含量：把水煮沸再过滤。

paras.en: In a study published Wednesday in Environmental Science & Technology Letters, researchers from China found that boiling tap water for just five minutes — then filtering it after it cools — could remove at least 80 percent of its microplastics.
paras.zh: 在周三发表于《环境科学与技术快报》的一项研究中，中国研究人员发现，把自来水煮沸仅五分钟，冷却后再过滤，就能去除其中至少80%的微塑料。

paras.en: Crucially, this process relies on the water containing enough calcium carbonate (碳酸钙) to trap the plastics.
paras.zh: 关键是，这个过程依赖于水中含有足够的碳酸钙来困住塑料。

w.m: adv. 关键是；至关重要的是

paras.en: In the study, boiling hard water containing 300 milligrams of calcium carbonate led to an almost 90 percent drop in plastics.
paras.zh: 研究中，煮沸含有300毫克碳酸钙的硬水后，塑料减少了近90%。

paras.en: But in samples with less than 60 milligrams of calcium carbonate, boiling reduced the level of plastics by just 25 percent.
paras.zh: 但在碳酸钙含量低于60毫克的样本中，煮沸只让塑料含量降低了25%。

paras.en: Additionally, the research didn’t include all types of plastics.
paras.zh: 此外，这项研究并没有涵盖所有种类的塑料。

paras.en: The team focused only on three common types — polystyrene, polyethylene and polypropylene — and they didn’t study other chemicals previously found in water such as vinyl chloride.
paras.zh: 研究团队只关注了三种常见类型——聚苯乙烯、聚乙烯和聚丙烯——也没有研究以前在水中发现的其他化学物质，比如氯乙烯。

paras.en: Still, the findings show a potential path forward for reducing microplastic exposure — a task that’s becoming increasingly difficult.
paras.zh: 不过，这些发现指明了一条减少微塑料暴露的潜在途径——而这项任务正变得越来越困难。

paras.en: Even bottled water, scientists found earlier this year, contains 10 to 1,000 times more microplastics than originally thought.
paras.zh: 今年早些时候，科学家们发现，就连瓶装水所含的微塑料也是原先认为的10到1000倍。

paras.en: Scientists are still trying to determine how harmful microplastics are — but what they do know has raised concerns.
paras.zh: 科学家们仍在努力确定微塑料的危害有多大——但他们确实了解到的情况已经引起了担忧。

paras.en: The new study suggests boiling tap water could be a tool to limit intake.
paras.zh: 这项新研究表明，把自来水煮沸或许可以成为限制微塑料摄入量的一种手段。

paras.en: “The way they demonstrated how microplastics were trapped through the boiling process was nice,” Caroline Gauchotte-Lindsay, an environmental engineer of the University of Glasgow in Scotland who was not involved in the research, tells New Scientist.
paras.zh: “他们展示微塑料如何在煮沸过程中被困住的方式很好，”未参与这项研究的苏格兰格拉斯哥大学环境工程师卡罗琳·高肖特-林赛对《新科学家》杂志表示。

paras.en: “We should be looking into upgrading drinking water treatment plants so they remove microplastics.”
paras.zh: “我们应该考虑升级饮用水处理厂，让它们能去除微塑料。”

passages.name: 2025 全国二卷 阅读C
passages.title: 养绿植让人身心更健康
passages.genre: 说明文 · 生活与健康
passages.summary: 人们居家时间增加，带动了室内绿植行业的爆发，一家网店仅 2020 年 6 月就发出 1200 单。研究者指出，身处绿植丰富环境中的人生活满意度更高，植物能降低压力激素皮质醇，让学生学习表现更好，让上班族病假减少 30%。作者提醒，植物养死了不必自责；店主也认为，养植物需要耐心和练习，用心照料，死了就再买一盆。

paras.en: When Sonja Detrinidad opened her online shop selling houseplants, she didn’t have high hopes for it.
paras.zh: 索尼娅·德特里尼达开网店卖室内绿植时，对这家店并没有抱太大希望。

paras.en: But the opposite happened: She was flooded, shipping out 1,200 orders in June of 2020 alone.
paras.zh: 但结果恰恰相反：订单如潮水般涌来，仅2020年6月一个月她就发货1200单。

w.m: v. 使应接不暇（此处为被动：订单如潮水般涌来）

paras.en: In the past year, Detrinidad sent out more than 70,000 plants.
paras.zh: 在过去一年里，德特里尼达寄出了7万多盆植物。

paras.en: Her success is just one example of increased time at home leading to an explosion in the houseplant industry.
paras.zh: 她的成功只是一个例子，说明居家时间增多引发了室内绿植行业的爆发式增长。

paras.en: “Plants are in fashion right now,” says Dr. Melinda Knuth, a researcher from the University of Florida.
paras.zh: “植物现在很流行，”佛罗里达大学的研究员梅林达·努斯博士说。

paras.en: “People who live in plant-rich environments report a higher life satisfaction rating,” she says.
paras.zh: “生活在绿植丰富环境中的人，自我报告的生活满意度评分更高，”她说。

paras.en: “Adding more nature to our environment can change our mood and how we think.”
paras.zh: “给我们的环境增添更多自然元素，可以改变我们的情绪和思维方式。”

paras.en: Plants can improve our state of mind in a few ways but the biggest is by decreasing our level of cortisol, the stress hormone (激素) in our body.
paras.zh: 植物可以从几个方面改善我们的精神状态，但最主要的一点是降低体内压力激素皮质醇的水平。

paras.en: “Students who are around plants perform better academically than students who are in a classroom without plants,” says Knuth.
paras.zh: “身边有植物的学生，学习成绩比在没有植物的教室里的学生更好，”努斯说。

paras.en: “This productivity also translates into the workplace for adults.
paras.zh: “对成年人来说，这种效率的提升同样体现在工作场所。

paras.en: Our study showed that there was a 30% decrease in sick leave for people who were in plant-rich workplaces.”
paras.zh: 我们的研究表明，在绿植丰富的工作场所，人们的病假减少了30%。”

paras.en: If you’re among the groups of people who are enjoying the mental and physical health benefits of surrounding yourself with plants, don’t beat yourself up if one (or a few!) doesn’t make it.
paras.zh: 如果你也属于那些正在享受被植物环绕所带来的身心健康益处的人，那么当一盆（或几盆！）没养活时，不要责怪自己。

paras.en: “Doctors practice medicine and lawyers practice law and you should allow yourself the practice it takes to sustain a plant.
paras.zh: “医生行医，律师从事法律工作，你也应该允许自己为养活一株植物而进行必要的练习。

paras.en: Tending to plants is an exercise in patience and learning.
paras.zh: 照料植物既是对耐心的锻炼，也是一个学习的过程。

paras.en: Be invested in taking care of it, but if it dies, go get another one,” Detrinidad says.
paras.zh: 用心照顾它，但如果它死了，就再去买一盆，”德特里尼达说。

passages.name: 2025 全国二卷 阅读D
passages.title: 用“废弃食材”做出的美味
passages.genre: 说明文 · 社会与环保
passages.summary: 食物浪费日益受到餐饮、超市和供应链行业的关注。纽约一家很受欢迎的餐厅曾更名为 wastED，为期两周，专门用通常会被扔掉的食材做菜，以唤起人们对食物浪费的关注。这些食材并非垃圾，而是大多数餐厅从不考虑使用的边角料，经一批优秀厨师之手变成了佳肴。这次短期实验提醒人们，解决可持续性问题有很多办法。

paras.en: Does your soul die a little every time you throw away unused food?
paras.zh: 每当你扔掉没吃的食物时，你的灵魂是否会有点难过？

paras.en: Mine does.
paras.zh: 我的就会。

paras.en: Maybe that feeling comes from growing up in South Africa, where the phrase “there are children starving in Africa” was more of an uncomfortable reminder of fact than a prayer at dinner time.
paras.zh: 也许这种感觉来自我在南非长大的经历，在那里，“非洲有孩子在挨饿”这句话与其说是晚餐时的祷告，不如说是对现实的一种令人不安的提醒。

paras.en: Food waste is a growing concern in the restaurant, supermarket, and supply chain industries.
paras.zh: 食物浪费日益成为餐饮、超市和供应链行业关注的问题。

paras.en: From technological solutions to educational campaigns, food producers and sellers are looking for ways to use more of what we’re already growing.
paras.zh: 从技术解决方案到教育活动，食品生产商和销售商都在寻找办法，更充分地利用我们已经种出来的东西。

paras.en: But last month, one popular New York City restaurant tried a different way: It changed its menu to exclusively (专门) offer food that would otherwise be thrown away.
paras.zh: 但上个月，纽约市一家很受欢迎的餐厅尝试了一种不同的方式：它更换了菜单，专门供应那些原本会被扔掉的食物。

w.m: adv. 否则；在其他情况下

paras.en: For two weeks in March, Greenwich Village’s Blue Hill restaurant was renamed wastED, and served items like fried skate cartilage, a juice pulp burger, and a dumpster diver’s vegetable salad.
paras.zh: 三月份的两周里，格林尼治村的蓝山餐厅更名为“wastED”，供应油炸鳐鱼软骨、果汁残渣汉堡和“翻垃圾箱者”蔬菜沙拉等菜品。

paras.en: Each dish was tailor-made to raise awareness regarding food waste.
paras.zh: 每道菜都是为提高人们对食物浪费的认识而量身定做的。

paras.en: A study by the Food Waste Alliance determined that the average restaurant generates 33 pounds of food waste for every $1,000 in revenue (收入), and of that waste only 15.7% is donated or recycled.
paras.zh: “食物浪费联盟”的一项研究发现，平均每家餐厅每创造1000美元收入，就会产生33磅食物垃圾，其中只有15.7%被捐赠或回收。

paras.en: Up to 84.3% is simply thrown out.
paras.zh: 多达84.3%被直接扔掉。

paras.en: Restaurants like Silo in the UK have experimented with zero-waste systems, but wastED took the concept to its logical conclusion.
paras.zh: 像英国的 Silo 这样的餐厅尝试过零浪费系统，但 wastED 把这一理念贯彻到底。

w.m: 把……贯彻到底；把……推向极致

paras.en: It should be noted that none of the items on wastED’s menu was technically made from garbage.
paras.zh: 需要指出的是，wastED 菜单上的菜品严格来说没有一样是用垃圾做的。

paras.en: Instead, all the ingredients (配料) used were examples of meat cuts and produce that most restaurants would never consider serving.
paras.zh: 相反，所用的食材都是大多数餐厅从来不会考虑供应的肉块和农产品。

paras.en: Things like kale ribs, fish collars, rejected sweet potatoes, and cucumber butts were all re-appropriated and, with the help of a number of good chefs, turned into excellent cuisine.
paras.zh: 像羽衣甘蓝茎、鱼颈肉、被淘汰的红薯和黄瓜蒂这样的东西都被重新利用，并在一批优秀厨师的帮助下，变成了精美的菜肴。

paras.en: Though wastED received enthusiastic reviews, it was designed from the start as a short-lived experiment; Blue Hill has since returned to its regular menu.
paras.zh: 尽管 wastED 好评如潮，但它从一开始就被设计成一次短期实验；此后蓝山餐厅已经恢复了常规菜单。

paras.en: Nevertheless, it serves as a reminder that there are many ways to address problems of sustainability, and that you can make an amazing meal out of almost anything.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，它提醒我们：解决可持续性问题的方法有很多，而且几乎用任何东西都能做出一顿美味佳肴。

passages.name: 2025 北京卷 阅读C
passages.title: 比较不一定是“快乐的窃贼”
passages.genre: 议论文 · 心理与家庭
passages.summary: 作者一直教孩子不要和别人比较，认为比较是“快乐的窃贼”，直到女儿用他的这条教诲反驳他。他反思后认为，社会比较既可能带来情绪困扰，也可以被利用来促进成长：和更优秀的人比可以化为动力，和处境更差的人比可以生出感恩。我们对自己的感受不仅取决于和谁比，还取决于怎么看待这种比较。

paras.en: Not too long ago, on a cold winter night, there was a teenager who wanted more screen time and a parent who said no.
paras.zh: 不久前的一个寒冷冬夜，一个青少年想多看一会儿屏幕，家长不同意。

paras.en: The teenager was advocating for her right to scroll (翻屏) for an extra 30 minutes.
paras.zh: 这个青少年正极力争取再多翻屏30分钟的权利。

paras.en: The parent argued that none of her friends’ parents let them have screens after 9 o’clock.
paras.zh: 家长争辩说，她朋友的父母都不允许孩子晚上9点以后看屏幕。

paras.en: “I thought, in this family, we don’t compare ourselves with other people, Dad?” the teenager replied.
paras.zh: “爸爸，我以为在我们家，我们不和别人比较呢？”这个青少年回答说。

paras.en: The parent — who was me, by the way — just got served.
paras.zh: 那位家长——顺便说一句，就是我——被将了一军。

paras.en: Since they were young, I have told my kids not to compare themselves with other people.
paras.zh: 从孩子们很小的时候起，我就告诉他们不要和别人比较。

paras.en: I have argued countless times that comparisons are the “thief of joy”.
paras.zh: 我无数次地说过，比较是“快乐的窃贼”。

paras.en: Although my daughter didn’t win, she did help expose one of the worst pieces of advice I have ever given.
paras.zh: 虽然我女儿没有赢，但她确实帮助揭露了我给过的最糟糕的建议之一。

paras.en: In my defence, I did what we’ve all done before, which is repeat received wisdom without exploring the nuances.
paras.zh: 为我自己辩解一句，我做了我们大家以前都做过的事，那就是重复人们普遍接受的观点，而没有去探究其中的细微差别。

w.m: 为某人辩护；为自己说句公道话

paras.en: But now is the time to set the record straight, which starts with questioning the idea that all social comparison is unhealthy.
paras.zh: 但现在是时候澄清事实了，首先就要质疑“所有社会比较都是不健康的”这一观点。

paras.en: Social comparisons do, of course, often get us into emotional trouble.
paras.zh: 当然，社会比较确实常常让我们陷入情绪困扰。

paras.en: But they can be harnessed (利用) for our betterment if we understand how they work.
paras.zh: 但如果我们了解它们的运作方式，就可以利用它们来让自己变得更好。

paras.en: The social comparisons we make — ones that lead us to feel good or bad about ourselves — are vital to our ability to thrive (成长).
paras.zh: 我们所做的社会比较——那些让我们自我感觉良好或糟糕的比较——对我们成长发展的能力至关重要。

paras.en: Science provides a guide we can use to harness the way we perform these comparisons to reduce their negative emotional impacts.
paras.zh: 科学提供了一份指南，我们可以用它来驾驭自己进行比较的方式，从而减少比较带来的负面情绪影响。

paras.en: Comparing yourself with someone who is outperforming you could result in feelings of envy if you focus on the things they have and you don’t, or it can be energizing and inspiring if you use these comparisons as a source of motivation, for example, “If they can achieve that, so can I.”
paras.zh: 和比你表现更好的人比较，如果你只盯着他们有而你没有的东西，就可能产生嫉妒；但如果你把这种比较当作动力来源，比如“他们能做到，我也能”，它就能让你充满干劲、受到鼓舞。

paras.en: Comparing yourself with someone who is doing worse than you could result in fear and worry if you think about how you could fall into similar circumstances, or it can draw out feelings of gratitude and appreciation if you use that comparison to broaden your views — for example, “Wow, things could be much worse; I’m doing great.”
paras.zh: 和比你境况更差的人比较，如果你去想自己会不会也落入类似的处境，就可能产生恐惧和担忧；但如果你借这种比较开阔视野，比如“哇，情况本可能糟得多，我已经过得很好了”，它就能唤起感激和感恩之情。

paras.en: What I wish I taught my daughter earlier are these nuances.
paras.zh: 我真希望当初早点教给女儿的，正是这些细微之处。

w.m: v. 真希望；要是……就好了（后接虚拟语气）

paras.en: How we feel about ourselves rests not just on whom we compare ourselves with but also on how we think about that comparison.
paras.zh: 我们对自己的感受，不仅取决于我们和谁比较，还取决于我们如何看待这种比较。

paras.en: That’s something we all have control over.
paras.zh: 这是我们每个人都能掌控的。

passages.name: 2025 北京卷 阅读D
passages.title: 改写人生故事，成为命运的作者
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理学
passages.summary: 心理学家提出身份认同的“人生故事”模型：从青少年时期起，我们围绕关键事件把人生组织成一个个章节，形成自己的故事，故事越连贯，身份感和人生意义感越强。研究发现，讲述往事时提到自己曾对事情有过一定掌控、能从压力事件中找到积极意义的人心理更健康，而且人可以学会改写自己的故事。也有学者提醒不要强求积极。选一个有意义的日子开启新“章节”会更有效。

paras.en: The call to “know yourself” has been there since ancient times, but our sense of self doesn’t always match what others perceive.
paras.zh: “认识你自己”的呼声自古就有，但我们的自我认知并不总是和别人看到的一致。

paras.en: Considering the stories we tell about ourselves can help us to change our minds for better.
paras.zh: 审视我们讲述自己的那些故事，可以帮助我们朝更好的方向改变想法。

paras.en: For many years psychologists saw identity as a combination of someone’s values, beliefs, goals and social roles.
paras.zh: 多年来，心理学家把身份认同看作一个人的价值观、信念、目标和社会角色的结合。

paras.en: Then, in the 1980s, Bob Johnson created the life story model of identity, in which he proposes that, as we go through life, these core features are built in with our memories to create a personal story through which we understand our lives.
paras.zh: 后来，在20世纪80年代，鲍勃·约翰逊创立了身份认同的“人生故事”模型。他在该模型中提出，在人生历程中，这些核心特征与我们的记忆融为一体，形成一个个人故事，我们借此理解自己的人生。

paras.en: Our life story is something that starts coming together in our teenage years, when we begin to organise our lives into chapters around key events or life changes, and begin to see ourselves as both the central character and, to a varying extent, the story’s author.
paras.zh: 我们的人生故事从青少年时期开始逐渐成形。那时，我们开始围绕关键事件或人生变化，把生活组织成一个个章节，并开始把自己既看作故事的主角，也在不同程度上看作故事的作者。

paras.en: People with more consistent stories tend to have a stronger sense of identity, and they feel their life has more meaning, direction and sense of purpose.
paras.zh: 故事更连贯的人往往身份感更强，他们觉得自己的人生更有意义、更有方向、更有目标感。

paras.en: Such people show greater overall life satisfaction, too.
paras.zh: 这样的人整体生活满意度也更高。

paras.en: Johnson has also investigated the link between well-being and certain story themes.
paras.zh: 约翰逊还研究了幸福感与某些故事主题之间的联系。

paras.en: He discovered that whether someone describes having had some control over events in their past is an important predictor of a person’s mental health.
paras.zh: 他发现，一个人是否描述自己曾对过去的事情有过一定的掌控，是预测其心理健康状况的重要指标。

paras.en: Another key theme involves finding some kind of positive meaning after stressful events.
paras.zh: 另一个关键主题是在经历压力事件后找到某种积极意义。

paras.en: “People could talk about gaining knowledge or personal growth,” says Johnson.
paras.zh: “人们可能会谈到收获了知识或个人成长，”约翰逊说。

paras.en: His research shows that this is often missing for people with mental health conditions.
paras.zh: 他的研究表明，有心理健康问题的人往往缺少这一点。

paras.en: The good news is that there is evidence we can learn to change our own story.
paras.zh: 好消息是，有证据表明我们可以学会改变自己的故事。

paras.en: Lisa Green, another researcher, sounds a few notes of caution (谨慎).
paras.zh: 另一位研究者丽莎·格林提醒人们，有几点需要谨慎。

w.m: 提醒（人们）要谨慎；提出告诫

paras.en: For instance, hearing about the power of redemptive (拯救性的) stories, many people may feel forced to find a positive angle on horrible events.
paras.zh: 例如，听说“救赎式”故事的力量后，许多人可能会觉得自己被迫要从可怕的事件中找出积极的一面。

paras.en: She says that Western culture already pushes people to look for the silver lining behind every cloud.
paras.zh: 她说，西方文化本来就在推动人们去寻找每片乌云背后的一线光明。

paras.en: If you want to turn over a new leaf, though, one top tip is that it helps to choose a significant date that signals the start of a new “chapter”.
paras.zh: 不过，如果你想重新开始，有一条绝佳的建议：选一个有意义的日子来标志新“章节”的开始，这会很有帮助。

paras.en: Contrary to popular doubt, resolutions made on 1 January are more effective for this reason.
paras.zh: 与人们普遍的怀疑相反，正因为这个原因，在1月1日立下的决心反而更有效。

paras.en: So, whether your goal is saving money or getting fit, there is no better time to become the author of our own destiny (命运).
paras.zh: 所以，无论你的目标是存钱还是健身，都没有比现在更好的时机来成为自己命运的作者了。

passages.name: 2025 天津卷（第二次·6月） 阅读C
passages.title: 海豹能感知血液中的氧气
passages.genre: 说明文 · 动物科学
passages.summary: 大多数哺乳动物靠血液中二氧化碳水平的升高来判断何时需要呼吸，但新研究表明海豹能直接感知血氧含量并据此调整潜水行为：呼吸室里的氧气含量越高，海豹在水下投食点停留得越久。人类似乎没有进化出感知低血氧的能力，这可能是不带氧气瓶的自由潜水事故频发的原因之一；反复潜水时依赖二氧化碳信号尤其危险。

paras.en: All animals take in oxygen from the air they breathe in, and release CO₂ from their blood when breathing out.
paras.zh: 所有动物都从吸入的空气中获取氧气，在呼气时把血液中的二氧化碳排出。

paras.en: Most mammals (哺乳动物) can’t directly detect oxygen levels in the blood supplied to their tissues.
paras.zh: 大多数哺乳动物无法直接察觉输送到身体组织的血液中的氧含量。

paras.en: Instead, they rely on the rising level of CO₂ in their blood to signal that they might need to take a breath.
paras.zh: 相反，它们依靠血液中不断升高的二氧化碳水平发出的信号，得知自己可能需要呼吸了。

paras.en: But a recent study published in Science suggests seals (海豹) can sense the amount of oxygen in the blood, and change their diving behavior in response.
paras.zh: 但发表在《科学》杂志上的一项最新研究表明，海豹能感知血液中的氧气含量，并据此改变潜水行为。

paras.en: To find out if oxygen levels affected seal behavior, Professor McKnight at the University of St. Andrews and his colleagues created a special section in a pool where young seals were held.
paras.zh: 为了弄清氧气水平是否会影响海豹的行为，圣安德鲁斯大学的麦克奈特教授和同事在饲养幼年海豹的水池中专门隔出了一块区域。

paras.en: In one corner, there was a breathing chamber (呼吸室), where they were sheltered from the rain and the wind.
paras.zh: 在一个角落里有一个呼吸室，海豹在那里可以躲避风雨。

paras.en: The breathing chamber was surrounded by panels that prevented surface swimming, yet swimming below the surface for about 200 feet would give the seals access to a feeder where they could eat as much fish as they liked.
paras.zh: 呼吸室四周围着挡板，使海豹无法在水面上游动；但如果在水面下游大约200英尺，海豹就能到达一个投食点，在那里想吃多少鱼就吃多少。

paras.en: Once the seals got familiar with the setup, the researchers started to gradually change the composition of the air in the breathing chamber, increasing or reducing the levels of oxygen and CO₂ to see an effect on their behavior.
paras.zh: 海豹熟悉了这一实验布置后，研究人员开始逐渐改变呼吸室内的空气成分，提高或降低氧气和二氧化碳的含量，看看这对它们的行为有什么影响。

paras.en: Sure enough: the higher the level of oxygen, the longer the seals stayed at the feeder.
paras.zh: 果然，氧气含量越高，海豹在投食点停留的时间就越长。

paras.en: The finding suggests that seals don’t just physically respond to oxygen levels by changing their heart rate or breathing, but that they are sufficiently aware of them to change their behavior.
paras.zh: 这一发现表明，海豹不只是在生理上通过改变心率或呼吸来对氧气水平做出反应，而且能足够清楚地察觉到氧气水平，从而改变自己的行为。

paras.en: This ability would put seals in a class beyond any land mammals that have been tested.
paras.zh: 这种能力会让海豹超越所有接受过测试的陆地哺乳动物。

paras.en: Since oxygen levels on land remain stable, humans don’t seem to have evolved (演化) to notice low blood oxygen levels, sometimes not even when they’re about to pass out in free-diving.
paras.zh: 由于陆地上的氧气水平保持稳定，人类似乎并没有进化出察觉血氧过低的能力，有时甚至在自由潜水中即将昏厥时也察觉不到。

paras.en: Therefore, in free-diving without oxygen tanks, accidents are quite common.
paras.zh: 因此，在不带氧气瓶的自由潜水中，事故相当常见。

paras.en: Our reliance on sensing CO₂ levels in our blood instead of oxygen may be to blame.
paras.zh: 我们依靠感知血液中的二氧化碳水平而不是氧气水平，这或许就是原因所在。

paras.en: Actually, this is a perfectly reasonable strategy on land, where growing CO₂ tends to signal breathing issues.
paras.zh: 其实，在陆地上这是一种完全合理的策略，因为在陆地上二氧化碳升高往往意味着呼吸出了问题。

paras.en: But when holding our breath during diving, relying on CO₂ levels is risky, especially on repeated dives.
paras.zh: 但在潜水时屏住呼吸的情况下，依靠二氧化碳水平是有风险的，尤其是在反复潜水时。

paras.en: Because every time we surface and breathe in, our sensitivity to CO₂ is decreased, even if its levels are already high, and this increases the chance that a person will, without awareness, pass out before they get to the surface.
paras.zh: 因为每次我们浮出水面吸气时，我们对二氧化碳的敏感度就会降低，即使它的含量已经很高；这就增加了一个人在毫无察觉的情况下，在到达水面之前昏厥的可能性。

passages.name: 2025 天津卷（第二次·6月） 阅读D

paras.en: Science serves as a powerful tool for unlocking the mysteries of the universe but understanding its limitations is essential for its effective application.
There are occasions where I have used the handle of a knife as a hammer (锤子), but the result would have been better if I’d had a more suitable tool at hand.
As far as science goes, it is really good at testing things that are testable, but not so for those that are not.
We can do, and have done, an impressive amount with our brains.
But there are limits.
Sometimes these limits go away if we keep at it for long enough — we just need better facilities and experiments to get the answer.
Breaking new ground in modern science this way can be costly.
Next-generation supercomputers or incredibly large telescopes are expensive, yet these may be required to find answers to some of the unsolved mysteries of the universe.
Sometimes the limits we encounter in trying to unlock the nature of the universe are cognitive (认知的).
Think about this: human DNA is only about 1.2 percent different from that of chimps (黑猩猩).
Chimps are smart, no question.
But could you teach them advanced mathematics?
What if our DNA were another 1.2 percent further evolved than it is?
What might our brains be capable of then?
The level of abstract thinking might be unimaginable.
Sometimes the limits we hit are fundamental.
There are laws of nature we may never be able to understand, however advanced our brains might become.
There are experiments we might never be able to perform.
We may never be able to test what caused the universe to be created, and what caused the cause of the universe being created.
This is where science may never break through.
For something to be considered scientific, it must, by definition, be testable.
There is a problem here: it may not need to be testable right now, but it must be testable at some point in the future by experiment.
If an idea is untestable, that doesn’t mean it is wrong.
It means it is untestable for now.
These untestable ideas also happen to be some of the most interesting ones, probably because they’ve puzzled humanity for centuries.
The pet food industry has received unkind remarks as to the true origin of its ingredients (原料) for decades.
Now the industry faces another source of criticism as a new book starts a debate about the environmental impact of owning a well-fed pet.

The New Scientist magazine, in a recent editorial, largely agreed with the book’s findings that some pets, due to the food they eat, have a surprisingly high “ecological footprint”, which is a way of quantifying human demand on the planet’s ecosystems using a measure called “global hectares”.
According to the authors of the book, “A shocking comparison is that in 2004, the average citizen of some poor countries had an eco-footprint of 0.76 hectares.
The eco-footprint of a cat is about 0.15 hectares, almost the same as what is needed to run a small car.
In a world where resources are already limited, can people really justify keeping pets that require more than some people?”
The authors of the book say that they were “genuinely surprised” when calculating the environmental impact of pets.
And some of the ideas they put forward to attenuate this are likely to shock some pet owners.
For example, the book suggests catching pests such as field mice and processing them into a “natural” cat food, or raising pets like chickens that provide both company and fresh eggs.
When feeding a pet, however, the advice is to favour pet foods made from chicken meat, which is less damaging to the environment than red meat and fish.

As you might expect, the Pet Food Manufacturers Association (PFMA) puts up a spirited defence, arguing that the vast majority of meat and fish used in pet foods is of sufficient quality for human consumption but more than humans need.
“If we didn’t recycle animal by-products to sell, they might instead be abandoned and buried under the earth, which is not very green,” says the director.
In addition, he points out that pets should not be viewed just on their carbon footprint.
“Our environment is greatly enriched by the part they play in our lives.
Pets in the home inspire responsibility, encourage social awareness and have positive health benefits.”

passages.name: 2026 全国Ⅰ卷 阅读C
passages.title: 纽约大规模种树的“隐患”
passages.genre: 说明文 · 环境科学
passages.summary: 纽约每年种下数万棵树，但新研究发现，占多数的橡树和枫香树会释放异戊二烯，它与车辆、建筑和工业排放的氮氧化物反应生成近地面臭氧，可能使空气质量变差。公园管理局的资深科学家认为不应把树当成敌人，更该反思以汽车为中心的生活方式。

paras.en: In line with longstanding initiatives to expand its green spaces, New York City is planting tens of thousands of trees each year.
paras.zh: 纽约市按照其长期以来推行的扩大绿地计划，每年都种植数以万计的树木。

paras.en: They provide shade, lower surface temperatures, absorb a surprising amount of airborne carbon, remove tiny pollutants, and provide wildlife habitat along with just plain beauty.
paras.zh: 它们提供树荫，降低地表温度，吸收空气中数量惊人的碳，清除微小的污染物，为野生动物提供栖息地，同时还带来纯粹的美感。

w.m: adj. 空气中的；大气中的

paras.en: Something could go wrong, though, according to a new study.
paras.zh: 不过，根据一项新研究，这当中可能会出问题。

paras.en: Oaks and sweetgums, which currently account for a majority of the city’s trees, produce huge amounts of a chemical substance called isoprene.
paras.zh: 橡树和枫香树目前占该市树木的大多数，它们会大量产生一种叫作异戊二烯的化学物质。

paras.en: Harmless by itself, isoprene interacts rapidly with polluting nitrogen oxides released by vehicles, buildings and industry to form ground-level ozone (臭氧) — a major factor in many breathing problems.
paras.zh: 异戊二烯本身无害，但它会与车辆、建筑和工业排放的污染性氮氧化物迅速发生反应，生成近地面臭氧——这是导致许多呼吸问题的一个主要因素。

w.m: v. 相互作用；发生反应
adj. 造成污染的；污染性的

paras.en: The research, carried out by scientists at the Columbia Climate School and other institutions, found that if the city maintains past species patterns in new plantings, isoprene production in Manhattan in coming decades will go up by about 140%, and resulting summer ozone levels as much as 30%.
paras.zh: 这项由哥伦比亚大学气候学院及其他机构的科学家开展的研究发现，如果该市在新栽种的树木中沿用过去的树种结构，未来几十年曼哈顿的异戊二烯产量将增加约140%，由此导致的夏季臭氧水平将上升多达30%。

w.m: adj. 由此产生的；随之而来的

paras.en: “We’re all for planting more trees.
paras.zh: “我们完全赞成多种树。

paras.en: They bring so many good things,” said study coauthor Róisín Commane.
paras.zh: 树木带来了那么多好处，”该研究的合著者罗欣·康曼说。

paras.en: “But if we’re not careful, we could make air quality worse.”
paras.zh: “但如果我们不小心，就可能让空气质量变得更糟。”

paras.en: The Parks Department is not oblivious to the issue.
paras.zh: 公园管理局并非没有意识到这个问题。

w.m: adj. 未察觉的；没意识到的

paras.en: A study carried out by some of its researchers several years ago concluded that city trees did release isoprene.
paras.zh: 几年前，该局的一些研究人员开展的一项研究就得出结论：城市树木确实会释放异戊二烯。

paras.en: “We didn’t make a big deal of that,” said Novem Auyeung, a Parks Department senior scientist.
paras.zh: “我们当时没有对此大做文章，”公园管理局的资深科学家诺文·欧阳说。

paras.en: She said trees should not be viewed as the enemy.
paras.zh: 她说，不应该把树木视为敌人。

paras.en: “We could plant any trees we want to, if we just rethink our car-centric lifestyle,” she said.
paras.zh: “只要我们重新审视以汽车为中心的生活方式，我们想种什么树都可以，”她说。

paras.en: “We’re not going to go cutting down any big old oaks,” and neither will the department completely stop planting new ones, said Auyeung.
paras.zh: “我们不会去砍掉任何高大的老橡树，”欧阳说，管理局也不会完全停止种植新的橡树。

paras.en: “You have to think about what you would lose if you do that.”
paras.zh: “你得想想，如果那样做，你会失去什么。”

paras.en: Oaks are keystone species, she pointed out, providing food and habitat for native insects, birds and other animals.
paras.zh: 她指出，橡树是关键物种，为本地的昆虫、鸟类和其他动物提供食物和栖息地。

passages.name: 2026 全国Ⅰ卷 阅读D
passages.title: 欣赏艺术之美能激发抽象思维
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理学研究
passages.summary: 剑桥心理学家在美术馆做实验：主动评判作品美感的一组，抽象思维得分比对照组平均高近14%（在有艺术爱好的人中，这一差距超过25%），而且更多地产生被感动、受启迪等“自我超越”感受；但他们并没有表示自己更快乐，说明起作用的是对美的投入。研究者认为欣赏美可能是开启抽象思维的理想方式。

paras.en: A team of Cambridge psychologists conducted an experiment to compare the cognitive (认知的) effects of merely seeing art with actively judging how beautiful it is.
paras.zh: 剑桥大学的一个心理学家团队开展了一项实验，比较仅仅观看艺术与主动评判艺术之美对认知产生的不同影响。

paras.en: In the study, 187 people were invited to visit Kettle’s Yard gallery during an exhibition of handmade clay objects.
paras.zh: 在研究中，187人受邀在一场手工陶土作品展期间参观了凯特尔庭院美术馆。

paras.en: Participants were randomly divided into two groups: the “beauty” group was asked to actively consider and then rate the beauty of each object they viewed, while the control group just matched a line drawing of the object with the artwork itself.
paras.zh: 参与者被随机分成两组：“美感组”被要求先主动思考所看到的每件作品的美，再给它打分；而对照组只需把作品的线描图和作品本身配对。

paras.en: All participants were then tested on how they process information, and whether it’s in a more practical or abstract way.
paras.zh: 随后，所有参与者都接受了测试，看他们如何处理信息，是更偏向实际的方式，还是更抽象的方式。

paras.en: Across all participants, those in the beauty group scored almost 14% higher on average than the control group in abstract thinking.
paras.zh: 从全体参与者来看，美感组在抽象思维上的得分平均比对照组高出近14%。

paras.en: While they were told the study was about cognitive processes, participants were asked about interests, with around half saying they had an artistic hobby.
paras.zh: 虽然参与者被告知这项研究是关于认知过程的，但他们也被问及兴趣爱好，约一半人说自己有艺术方面的爱好。

paras.en: Among those, the effect was greater: those with an artistic hobby in the beauty group scored over 25% higher on average for abstract thinking than those with an artistic hobby in the control group.
paras.zh: 在这些人当中，效果更明显：美感组中有艺术爱好的人，抽象思维平均得分比对照组中有艺术爱好的人高出25%以上。

paras.en: Emotional states of participants were also measured by asking about their feelings while completing the gallery task.
paras.zh: 研究人员还通过询问参与者完成美术馆任务时的感受，测量了他们的情绪状态。

paras.en: Across all participants, those in the beauty group reported an average of 23% higher levels of “transformative and self-transcendent feelings” — such as feeling moved, enlightened and inspired — than the control group.
paras.zh: 从全体参与者来看，美感组报告的“使人转变和自我超越的感受”（比如被感动、受启迪、受鼓舞）的程度平均比对照组高出23%。

paras.en: Importantly, however, the beauty group did not report feeling any happier than the control group, suggesting that it was the engagement with beauty that influenced abstract thinking, rather than any overall positivity from the experience.
paras.zh: 但重要的是，美感组并没有表示自己比对照组更快乐，这说明影响抽象思维的是对美的投入，而不是这次体验带来的整体积极情绪。

paras.en: “We usually think in very concrete terms when doing something on a screen,” said Simone Schnall, senior author of the study.
paras.zh: “我们在屏幕上做事时，通常是用非常具体的方式思考，”该研究的资深作者西蒙娜·施纳尔说。

paras.en: “It’s becoming much rarer to zone out and just let the mind wander, but that’s when we think in ways that broaden our minds.
paras.zh: “放空自己、任思绪漫游的时候已经变得少多了，但恰恰是在那种时候，我们会以开阔思维的方式去思考。

paras.en: Admiring the beauty of art may be the ideal way to initiate the abstract cognitive processes.”
paras.zh: 欣赏艺术之美，可能是开启抽象认知过程的理想方式。”

passages.name: 2026 全国Ⅱ卷 阅读C
passages.title: 海拔的“零点”：海平面概念的历史
passages.genre: 说明文 · 书籍序言
passages.summary: 作者指出海拔是相对的，必须有参照点；而“海平面”这个参照点本身是由技术和文化所决定的种种假设的产物，是一个有自己历史的概念。他在山中徒步时因测高仪读数不一致而萌生写书的念头，书中考察了平均海平面历史上的三个关键阶段，并指出海平面上升问题日益紧迫。

paras.en: The peak of Mount Qomolangma, 8,849 meters above sea level.
paras.zh: 珠穆朗玛峰峰顶，海拔8849米。

paras.en: Chimborazo, 6,263 m; Mont Blanc, 4,806 m; Pradidali hut, at the foot of the Pala group in the Dolomites, 2,278 m.
paras.zh: 钦博拉索山，6263米；勃朗峰，4806米；位于多洛米蒂山脉帕拉山群脚下的普拉迪达利小屋，2278米。

paras.en: It is common practice to provide the elevation (高度) of a place.
paras.zh: 标出一个地方的海拔高度是一种常见做法。

paras.en: Simple readings are now readily available on our phones and wearables.
paras.zh: 如今，在手机和可穿戴设备上就能轻松获取简单的读数。

paras.en: But elevation is necessarily relative: only the choice of a reference point allows us to express numerically the height of an object or a location.
paras.zh: 但海拔必然是相对的：只有选定一个参照点，我们才能用数字表示某个物体或地点的高度。

paras.en: The idea of sea level as a reference point for elevations has by now been around for so long as to go essentially unnoticed — we mention it without even considering what it means.
paras.zh: 把海平面作为海拔参照点的观念由来已久，以至于基本上没人注意到它——我们提到它时，甚至都不会去想它意味着什么。

paras.en: That the concept has a history is easily ignored.
paras.zh: 这个概念有它自己的历史，这一点很容易被忽视。

paras.en: We tend to forget that sea level is a product of technically and culturally determined assumptions.
paras.zh: 我们往往会忘记，海平面是由技术和文化所决定的种种假设的产物。

paras.en: In this book, I tell a story of these assumptions.
paras.zh: 在这本书中，我讲述的就是这些假设的故事。

paras.en: Appropriately, the book took shape during a summer spent between sea and mountains.
paras.zh: 颇为应景的是，这本书是在一个于海边和山间度过的夏天里成形的。

w.m: adv. 恰当地；（修饰全句）应景地

paras.en: A month after visiting the French Riviera and enjoying the sandy beaches of Nice and Menton, I went hiking with friends in the Pala group.
paras.zh: 游览法国里维埃拉、享受过尼斯和芒通的沙滩之后，过了一个月，我和朋友们去帕拉山群徒步。

paras.en: Resting on a pass near the Pradidali hut, we began discussing the readings offered by our altimeters (测高仪).
paras.zh: 在普拉迪达利小屋附近的一处山口休息时，我们开始讨论各自测高仪给出的读数。

paras.en: Why did they vary ever so slightly from one instrument to the next?
paras.zh: 为什么不同仪器之间的读数会有那么一丁点差异呢？

paras.en: This sense of uncertainty led me to think about the meaning of zero.
paras.zh: 这种不确定感促使我思考“零”的含义。

paras.en: This is how I began my search for the conceptual history of sea level.
paras.zh: 我就是这样开始探寻海平面这一概念的历史的。

paras.en: In this book I examine three crucial stages in the history of mean sea level.
paras.zh: 在本书中，我考察了平均海平面历史上的三个关键阶段。

paras.en: These stages mirror the development of human conceptions of the sea.
paras.zh: 这些阶段反映了人类对海洋认识的发展。

paras.en: Since I began thinking about this project in August 2011, the issue of sea-level rise and the need to place it historically have only become more urgent: between then and the end of 2022 the global sea rose by almost 5 centimeters, about half of the overall rise recorded by satellites since 1993.
paras.zh: 自2011年8月我开始构思这个项目以来，海平面上升问题以及从历史角度看待它的必要性都变得愈发紧迫：从那时到2022年底，全球海平面上升了近5厘米，约为1993年以来卫星记录的总上升幅度的一半。

passages.name: 2026 全国Ⅱ卷 阅读D
passages.title: 地铁刹车给电动汽车充电
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与环保
passages.summary: 巴塞罗那推出 MetroCharge 项目：地铁列车刹车时回收的能量，一部分供列车和车站使用，剩余部分通过电缆送到地面，为附近的电动汽车充电。一位拥有电动汽车的乘客对此感到惊喜，专家认为它把回收能量用于本地特定用途，提高了能源利用效率。

paras.en: The Barcelona subway pulls into the station, the doors slide open and passengers pour out to go about their daily business.
paras.zh: 巴塞罗那的地铁驶进车站，车门滑开，乘客们涌出车厢，去忙各自的日常事务。

paras.en: Little do they know that as they do so, a burst of energy is sent up to street level to help charge an electric car.
paras.zh: 他们根本不知道，就在他们这样做的时候，一股能量正被输送到街面上，帮一辆电动汽车充电。

paras.en: Barcelona has put together a package of clean energy technologies to help public transportation go greener, while also doing its part to tackle climate change and aid Europe’s difficult shift to the privately owned electric vehicle market.
paras.zh: 巴塞罗那整合了一整套清洁能源技术，让公共交通更环保，同时也为应对气候变化出一份力，并助力欧洲向私人电动汽车市场的艰难转型。

w.m: n. 一整套（相关事物）；一揽子

paras.en: Sixteen stations of Barcelona’s subway system are part of its new MetroCharge project, whereby the energy from the underground trains’ brakes (刹车) is used to power the trains and the stations themselves, while the remainder is sent snaking through cables (电缆) to the surface to power plug-in stations for privately owned vehicles.
paras.zh: 巴塞罗那地铁系统的16个车站加入了新的MetroCharge（“地铁充电”）项目：地下列车刹车产生的能量被用来为列车和车站本身供电，剩余部分则通过蜿蜒的电缆输送到地面，为私家车的插电式充电桩供电。

w.m: v. 为……供电；为……提供动力

paras.en: Bernardo Espinoza, an engineer who takes the subway every day, owns an electric car.
paras.zh: 贝尔纳多·埃斯皮诺萨是一名每天乘坐地铁的工程师，他有一辆电动汽车。

paras.en: “I am pleasantly surprised, because I am always looking for where to plug it in,” Espinoza said before catching the subway in a working-class area of southern Barcelona.
paras.zh: “我感到惊喜，因为我总是在找地方给它充电，”埃斯皮诺萨在巴塞罗那南部一个工人阶层聚居区赶地铁前说道。

paras.en: “And if it is from energy from the trains’ brakes, then even better.”
paras.zh: “如果电来自列车刹车的能量，那就更好了。”

paras.en: Regenerative brakes have been in trains for decades and are also used in some cars.
paras.zh: 再生制动器在列车上已经使用了几十年，一些汽车上也有应用。

w.m: adj. 再生的；回收能量的

paras.en: They consist of an electric motor which collects energy used in the braking action that would be lost as heat by conventional brakes.
paras.zh: 它们由一台电动机构成，电动机收集刹车过程中的能量，而这些能量在传统刹车中会以热量的形式散失。

paras.en: That energy can be immediately used to accelerate (加速) the vehicle or, in the case of the Barcelona subway system, sent along cables to supply electricity for the station or for electric car chargers.
paras.zh: 这些能量可以立即用来给车辆加速；或者，就巴塞罗那地铁系统而言，通过电缆输送，为车站或电动汽车充电桩供电。

paras.en: Alvaro Luna, a professor of electrical engineering, said that the system is innovative in so far as it allows for recycled energy to be redirected to specific local uses — in this case powering electric cars parked nearby.
paras.zh: 电气工程学教授阿尔瓦罗·卢纳说，这个系统的创新之处在于，它让回收的能量能够被重新引导，用于本地的特定用途——在这里就是为停在附近的电动汽车供电。

paras.en: That, he said, boosts efficiency.
paras.zh: 他说，这提高了效率。

passages.name: 2026 北京卷 阅读C
passages.title: 气候变化正在改变世界的“气味景观”
passages.genre: 说明文 · 环境与文化
passages.summary: 气味常被忽视，但高温和污染正在改变世界的“气味景观”：气温升高使人造物质释放更多气味分子，生物多样性丧失可能让某些气味彻底消失，雪那原本清冷干净的气味也会因气候变暖而改变，变得更难闻。有些气味还与文化遗产相连，比如秘鲁原住民注意到亚马孙河气味的变化。作者呼吁重视气味背后的文化价值。

paras.en: Smells are all around us.
paras.zh: 气味无处不在。

paras.en: What we know as a scent (气味) is a collection of natural or artificial airborne chemicals released from objects.
paras.zh: 我们所说的气味，是从物体中释放出来的、飘散在空气中的天然或人造化学物质的集合。

paras.en: But smell is often overlooked and undervalued.
paras.zh: 但嗅觉常常被忽视，也被低估。

paras.en: So, as climate change and biodiversity loss threaten natural scents, many people may not even notice.
paras.zh: 因此，当气候变化和生物多样性丧失威胁到自然界的气味时，许多人甚至可能察觉不到。

paras.en: Whether or not we pay attention to the world’s “scentscape”, heat and pollution are causing it to shift.
paras.zh: 无论我们是否留意世界的“气味景观”，高温和污染都在使它发生变化。

paras.en: As temperatures rise, man-made substances release more scent molecules (分子), and biodiversity loss due to climate change threatens the plants that scent the environment.
paras.zh: 随着气温升高，人造物质会释放更多的气味分子；而气候变化导致的生物多样性丧失，也威胁着那些为环境增添气味的植物。

paras.en: “If you go to a forest, you have a given environment and temperature.
paras.zh: “如果你走进一片森林，那里有特定的环境和温度。

paras.en: If that temperature goes a little bit high, the profile of the chemical components in the air changes,” since temperature can affect the amount of smell-carrying gas particles (粒子) released from substances, explains John Smith, a chemical engineer.
paras.zh: 如果温度升高一点，空气中化学成分的构成就会改变，”化学工程师约翰·史密斯解释说，这是因为温度会影响物质释放出的、携带气味的气体粒子的数量。

paras.en: “And therefore, the perception of how the forest smells changes.”
paras.zh: “因此，人们对这片森林气味的感知也会改变。”

paras.en: That effect extends beyond forests.
paras.zh: 这种影响不仅限于森林。

paras.en: Snow — already threatened by a warming climate — absorbs different chemicals from the atmosphere as temperatures rise, which changes its cold-clean scent.
paras.zh: 雪本身已经受到气候变暖的威胁；随着气温升高，雪会从大气中吸收不同的化学物质，这会改变它那种清冷干净的气味。

paras.en: Warmer conditions can intensify smells, leading the snow to smell more unpleasant and potentially gather more pollutants.
paras.zh: 更温暖的环境会使气味变得更浓，让雪的气味更难闻，还可能让雪聚集更多的污染物。

paras.en: Climate change is also quickening the loss of biodiversity, threatening to erase certain smells entirely.
paras.zh: 气候变化还在加速生物多样性的丧失，可能会让某些气味彻底消失。

paras.en: When plants disappear, their scents become more difficult to produce.
paras.zh: 植物消失了，它们的气味也就更难产生了。

paras.en: Some scents are linked to cultural heritage.
paras.zh: 有些气味与文化遗产相关。

paras.en: A recent study reported that native communities in Peru noticed a change in the smell of the Amazon River due to industrial pollution.
paras.zh: 最近的一项研究报告称，秘鲁的原住民社区注意到，由于工业污染，亚马孙河的气味发生了变化。

paras.en: Over generations, communities became desensitised to increasingly smelly rivers, a sign of broader ecosystem degradation.
paras.zh: 一代又一代人下来，这些社区对越来越难闻的河流变得麻木了——河流越来越难闻，是生态系统更大范围退化的一个迹象。

paras.en: At the same time, in some Amazonian belief systems, declining water quality and the unpleasant smells will lead to the dispersal (消散) of the river’s spiritual beings.
paras.zh: 与此同时，在亚马孙地区的一些信仰体系中，水质下降和难闻的气味会导致河中的神灵消散。

paras.en: The damage to the scentscape could result in harm to both health and spiritual practice.
paras.zh: 对气味景观的破坏，可能会同时危害人们的健康和精神信仰活动。

w.m: n. （宗教、信仰等的）惯常活动；习俗

paras.en: Even though we have other valuable things endangered by climate change, like food access, there is also an element of cultural identity, cultural survival, and history.
paras.zh: 尽管还有其他宝贵的东西受到气候变化的威胁，比如获取食物的途径，但气味中也包含着文化认同、文化存续和历史的元素。

paras.en: If we don’t look at it, we lose all the richness behind it.
paras.zh: 如果我们不去关注它，就会失去它背后的全部丰富内涵。

passages.name: 2026 北京卷 阅读D
passages.title: 别急着拆掉那道“篱笆”
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与思维
passages.summary: 近二三十年，“颠覆者”成了人们谈论商界时一个为人熟知的形象，其态度可概括为“快速行动，打破常规”。作者借切斯特顿的“篱笆”思想实验指出：看不出一道篱笆的用处，恰恰是不该拆它的理由。改革并非不可以，但应先理解过去决定中的智慧。我们需要的不是无所畏惧，而是停下来提问的谦卑。

paras.en: The 21st century has created a whole range of new types of professionals that we have never had before — or if not quite new, at least newly repackaged.
paras.zh: 21世纪造就了各种各样我们以前从未有过的新型职业人士——即便不算全新，至少也是换了新包装。

w.m: n. 专业人士；职业人士

paras.en: The world has always had influential people, for instance, but only now do we have “Influencer”.
paras.zh: 比如，世界上一直都有有影响力的人，但直到现在我们才有了“网红”这个称呼。

w.m: n. 网红；有影响力的人

paras.en: Similarly, the corporate world has certainly known its fair share of disruption, yet it is only in the last couple of decades that the “Disruptor” has become a recognisable figure in the way we talk about big business.
paras.zh: 同样，企业界当然经历过不少颠覆，但直到最近二三十年，“颠覆者”才成为我们谈论大企业时一个为人熟知的人物形象。

w.m: adj. 可辨认的；易于识别的；为人熟知的

paras.en: In an earlier era, the Disruptor would have been called an Innovator.
paras.zh: 在更早的年代，“颠覆者”会被称为“创新者”。

paras.en: Yet while an Innovator creates something new, the Disruptor is defined as much by what they destroy as by what they create.
paras.zh: 然而，创新者创造新事物，而颠覆者既由他们创造的东西来定义，也同样由他们摧毁的东西来定义。

paras.en: The Disruptor forces change; the clean-up is somebody else’s problem.
paras.zh: 颠覆者强行推动变革，至于收拾残局，那是别人的事。

w.m: v. 强行推动；强行促成

paras.en: It’s an attitude best summed up as “Move fast and break things.”
paras.zh: 用一句话来概括这种态度最贴切：“快速行动，打破常规。”

paras.en: Back in 1929, G. K. Chesterton identified the core problem with moving fast and breaking things through a thought experiment.
paras.zh: 早在1929年，G. K. 切斯特顿就通过一个思想实验，指出了“快速行动，打破常规”的核心问题。

paras.en: Imagine there is a fence along a road.
paras.zh: 想象一下，路边有一道篱笆。

paras.en: Suppose it’s been there a long time, and was put there for some purpose.
paras.zh: 假设它已经在那里很久了，而且当初是为了某个目的修建的。

paras.en: But that purpose is lost over time.
paras.zh: 但随着时间推移，那个目的被遗忘了。

paras.en: To us, now, the fence seems to be nothing but an impediment.
paras.zh: 对现在的我们来说，这道篱笆似乎只是个障碍。

paras.en: Why not remove it?
paras.zh: 为什么不把它拆掉呢？

paras.en: When faced with such a fence, Chesterton thinks the fact that we can’t see the point of the fence is why we should not tear it down.
paras.zh: 切斯特顿认为，面对这样一道篱笆，我们看不出它有什么用，这恰恰是我们不该拆掉它的理由。

paras.en: Some fences keep foxes out of henhouses, for instance.
paras.zh: 比如，有些篱笆是为了把狐狸挡在鸡舍外面。

paras.en: If you think you can do without the fence because you’ve never seen a fox, consider if the existence of the fence is precisely why you’ve never seen one.
paras.zh: 如果你因为从没见过狐狸，就认为没有篱笆也行，那就想想：你从没见过狐狸，是不是恰恰因为有这道篱笆。

paras.en: Importantly, Chesterton is not saying that things can never be reformed.
paras.zh: 重要的是，切斯特顿并不是说事物永远不能改革。

paras.en: His is a preventive principle rather than an outright prohibition.
paras.zh: 他提出的是一个预防性原则，而不是彻底的禁令。

paras.en: We could rephrase it like this: understand the wisdom in past decisions before you reject them.
paras.zh: 我们可以这样换个说法：在否定过去的决定之前，先理解其中的智慧。

paras.en: If we’re too impetuous, we can end up tearing out things we don’t yet realise we rely upon.
paras.zh: 如果我们过于冲动，最后可能会拆掉一些我们还没意识到自己依赖着的东西。

paras.en: But uncritical devotion to the “way things are done” can also deny us the possibility of better days.
paras.zh: 但对“做事的老规矩”不加批判地一味奉行，也可能让我们失去迎来更好日子的可能性。

paras.en: What is required, then, is not the fearlessness of the Disruptor, but the humility (谦卑) to stop and ask questions and to know that our own perspective is neither unique nor comprehensive.
paras.zh: 那么，我们需要的不是颠覆者那种无所畏惧，而是一种谦卑：停下来提问，并且明白我们自己的视角既不是唯一的，也不是全面的。

w.m: adj. 唯一的；独一无二的

paras.en: Disruption can be a force for good.
paras.zh: 颠覆可以成为一种积极的力量。

paras.en: It can also just leave a big mess.
paras.zh: 它也可能只留下一个大烂摊子。

paras.en: We need the ability to work out which messes are worth avoiding — because however impressively fast you move, some things can’t be easily unbroken.
paras.zh: 我们需要有能力判断哪些烂摊子值得避免——因为无论你行动的速度快得多么惊人，有些东西一旦被破坏就不容易复原。

w.m: v. 使复原；使恢复原状（此处为被动 be unbroken）

passages.name: 2026 天津卷（第一次·3月） 阅读C
passages.title: 我不想再谈“女科学家”这个身份
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人物与观点
passages.summary: 一位天体物理学家回顾：年轻时她并不在意自己是课堂上唯一的女生，后来每一项成就和失败都被放在性别政治的视角下审视，她也曾为此激烈争辩。如今她不再谈论性别话题，而是专注于自己热爱的科学；在她任教的女子学院里，她班上的 45 名学生全是女性，她用自己怀孕时仍做物理实验的形象激励学生。

paras.en: I don’t ever want to talk about being a woman scientist again.
paras.zh: 我再也不想谈论身为女科学家这件事了。

paras.en: There was a time in my life when people asked constantly for stories about what it’s like to work in a field dominated by men.
paras.zh: 我人生中曾有一段时间，人们总是请我讲些故事，讲讲在男性主导的领域工作是什么感受。

paras.en: I was never very good at telling those stories because truthfully I never found them interesting.
paras.zh: 我从来都不太会讲这些故事，因为说实话，我从来不觉得它们有意思。

paras.en: What I do find interesting is the origin of the universe, the shape of space-time and the nature of black holes.
paras.zh: 我真正感兴趣的，是宇宙的起源、时空的形态和黑洞的本质。

paras.en: At 19, when I began studying astrophysics, it did not bother me in the least to be the only woman in the classroom.
paras.zh: 19岁开始学天体物理时，我是教室里唯一的女生，但我对此一点也不在意。

paras.en: But while earning my Ph.D. at MIT and then as a post-doctor doing space research, the issue started to bother me.
paras.zh: 但在麻省理工学院读博士期间，以及后来做太空研究的博士后时，这个问题开始困扰我。

paras.en: My every achievement—jobs, research papers, awards—was viewed through the lens of gender (性别) politics.
paras.zh: 我的每一项成就——工作、研究论文、奖项——都被放在性别政治的视角下审视。

paras.en: So were my failures.
paras.zh: 我的失败也是如此。

paras.en: Sometimes, when I was pushed into an argument on left brain versus (相对于) right brain, or nature versus nurture (培育), I would instantly fight fiercely on my behalf and all womankind.
paras.zh: 有时，当我被卷入关于左脑与右脑、先天与后天的争论时，我会立刻为自己、也为全体女性激烈地争辩。

w.m: 为了某人（的利益）；代表某人

paras.en: Then one day a few years ago, out of my mouth came a sentence that would eventually become my reply to any and all provocations: I don’t talk about that anymore.
paras.zh: 后来，几年前的一天，我脱口说出了一句话，这句话最终成了我对一切挑衅的回答：我不再谈论那个话题了。

paras.en: It took me 10 years to get back the confidence I had at 19 and to realize that I didn’t want to deal with gender issues.
paras.zh: 我花了10年时间，才找回19岁时的那份自信，并意识到自己不想去应付性别问题。

paras.en: Why should curing sexism be yet another terrible burden on every female scientist?
paras.zh: 为什么消除性别歧视要成为每一位女科学家的又一个沉重负担？

paras.en: After all, I don’t study sociology or political theory.
paras.zh: 毕竟，我研究的又不是社会学或政治理论。

paras.en: Today I research and teach at Barnard, a women’s college in New York City.
paras.zh: 如今，我在巴纳德学院——纽约市的一所女子学院——做研究并授课。

paras.en: Recently, someone asked me how many of the 45 students in my class were women.
paras.zh: 最近，有人问我班上45名学生中有多少是女生。

paras.en: You cannot imagine my satisfaction at being able to answer, 45.
paras.zh: 你想象不到，我能回答“45名”时有多满足。

paras.en: I know some of my students worry how they will manage their scientific research and a desire for children.
paras.zh: 我知道，我的一些学生担心将来如何兼顾科研和想要孩子的愿望。

paras.en: And I don’t dismiss those concerns.
paras.zh: 我并不轻视这些顾虑。

paras.en: Still, I don’t tell them “war” stories.
paras.zh: 不过，我不会给她们讲那些“战斗”故事。

paras.en: Instead, I have given them this: the visual of their physics professor heavily pregnant doing physics experiments.
paras.zh: 相反，我给了她们这样一个画面：她们的物理教授挺着大肚子做物理实验。

paras.en: And in turn they have given me the image of 45 women driven by a love of science.
paras.zh: 反过来，她们也给了我这样一幅图景：45名女性因热爱科学而奋进。

paras.en: And that’s a sight worth talking about.
paras.zh: 这才是值得一谈的景象。

passages.name: 2026 天津卷（第一次·3月） 阅读D
passages.title: 无人问津的视频，藏着互联网的另一面
passages.genre: 说明文 · 网络与社会
passages.summary: YouTube 对外展示的是专业、热闹的形象，但换个角度看，它的本质更像那些几乎无人观看的普通视频，比如一段在作者观看之前只被看过两次、19 分钟里什么也没发生的窗外雪景。研究者指出，只关注热门内容，就会看不到绝大多数人作为上传者实际上是如何使用 YouTube 的。抖音、快手上也有大量质朴的自我表达，它们不受算法塑造，是人们存放在“数字阁楼”里的记忆，看得足够多就能拼凑出特定地区、特定时期的生活面貌，让人看到互联网仍有希望的一面。

paras.en: On 23 April 2005, YouTube posted its first video.
paras.zh: 2005年4月23日，YouTube 发布了它的第一个视频。

paras.en: 20 years later, YouTube is the world’s number one streaming service, where users clock billions of hours of watching every day.
paras.zh: 20年后，YouTube 成为全球第一的流媒体服务平台，用户每天在上面观看的时长累计达数十亿小时。

paras.en: That’s the vision of YouTube the company promotes — professional, entertaining and loud — but from one perspective, it’s all a facade.
paras.zh: 这是该公司对外推广的 YouTube 形象——专业、有趣又热闹——但从某个角度看，这全是表象。

paras.en: Through another lens, the essence of YouTube is more like this video from 2020.
paras.zh: 换个角度看，YouTube 的本质更像是2020年的这段视频。

paras.en: Before I watched, it had only been seen twice.
paras.zh: 在我观看之前，它只被看过两次。

paras.en: A man points the camera out of his bedroom window as the winter snow falls.
paras.zh: 一个男人把镜头对着卧室窗外，外面正下着冬雪。

paras.en: “Here it is,” he says.
paras.zh: “就是这个，”他说。

paras.en: “The falling snow.”
paras.zh: “飘落的雪。”

paras.en: A bird lands on a nearby fence.
paras.zh: 一只鸟落在附近的篱笆上。

paras.en: 19 minutes go by.
paras.zh: 19分钟过去了。

paras.en: Nothing happens.
paras.zh: 什么也没发生。

paras.en: When we just focus on what’s popular, we miss how the vast majority of people actually use YouTube as uploaders, and overlook the role it plays in our society, says Ryan McGrady, a senior researcher.
paras.zh: 资深研究员瑞安·麦格雷迪说，当我们只关注热门内容时，就会看不到绝大多数人作为上传者实际上是如何使用 YouTube 的，也会忽视它在我们社会中所起的作用。

paras.en: This is not just the case with YouTube but with every major online video platform around the world.
paras.zh: 不只是 YouTube，世界上每一个主要的在线视频平台都是如此。

paras.en: For example, if you spend some time dipping into the corners of Douyin and Kuaishou, two of China’s most popular online video apps, you could see a side of the Internet that sometimes feels lost, one full of pure, unvarnished (质朴的) self-expression.
paras.zh: 比如，抖音和快手同属中国最受欢迎的在线视频应用之列，如果你花些时间到这两个平台的角落里随意翻看，就能看到互联网有时让人觉得已经消失的一面——这一面充满了纯粹、质朴的自我表达。

w.m: adj. 质朴的；不加修饰的

paras.en: It’s an entire world that the algorithm (算法) won’t show you.
paras.zh: 那是算法不会展示给你的一整个世界。

paras.en: Most of these videos are poorly produced, lack context or just meaninglessly show this and that.
paras.zh: 这些视频大多制作粗糙，缺乏背景交代，或者只是毫无意义地拍拍这个、拍拍那个。

paras.en: They exist because people need a digital attic to store their memories.
paras.zh: 它们之所以存在，是因为人们需要一个数字阁楼来存放自己的记忆。

paras.en: It’s an Internet unshaped by the pressures of algorithms — a glimpse into a place where content doesn’t have to perform, where it can simply exist.
paras.zh: 这是一个不受算法压力塑造的互联网——让人得以一窥这样一个地方：在那里，内容不必刻意表现，可以只是单纯地存在。

paras.en: And perhaps the most important thing about these videos is that if you watch enough of them, you can piece together a complete narrative of life, work, and society in a specific region and time period.
paras.zh: 而这些视频最重要的一点或许是：只要你看得足够多，就能拼凑出某个特定地区、特定时期的生活、工作和社会的完整叙事。

paras.en: This knowledge could be — and sometimes is — more valuable than a book or an online class.
paras.zh: 这种知识可能——有时确实——比一本书或一门网课更有价值。

paras.en: “The Internet is deeply troubled, and we can’t ignore the way tech companies are exacerbating (使恶化) those problems,” McGrady says.
paras.zh: “互联网问题重重，我们不能无视科技公司是如何让这些问题不断恶化的，”麦格雷迪说。

w.m: adj. 有问题的；问题重重的

paras.en: “What makes me hopeful is that when you find a way to look at how people are really using the web, a lot of it still feels like the early Internet.
paras.zh: “让我感到有希望的是，当你找到方法去观察人们真正是如何使用网络的时候，会发现其中很多内容仍然像早期的互联网。

w.m: adj. 抱有希望的；充满希望的

paras.en: It’s expression, communication, and connection.
paras.zh: 那是表达、交流和联结。

paras.en: Fundamentally, it’s a place where regular people share themselves and do wonderful things.”
paras.zh: 从根本上说，这是一个普通人分享自我、做美好事情的地方。”
